title: observability: add token-level KV cost/latency dashboard and alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: operators and platform teams need token-level visibility into KV cache effectiveness, per-token latency and unit cost to tune batching and cache policies. This PR introduces a Grafana dashboard and backend metric instrumentation to surface token-level KV hits/misses, per-token latency distribution, and a derived token-cost estimate that combines GPU token-time with billing rates.

What I changed: - Added Prometheus metrics in serving/runtime: redwood_kv_token_hits_total, redwood_kv_token_misses_total, redwood_kv_token_latency_seconds_bucket (histogram), redwood_token_compute_time_seconds (per-token). - Exposed a derived metric redwood_token_cost_usd computed in the metrics pipeline (PromQL example included in docs). - New Grafana dashboard JSON with panels for cost/latency breakdowns, KV hit heatmap, heavy prefix contributors, and per-model breakdowns. - Alert rules tuned: high token_cost (5m sustained) and low kv_hit_rate regressions (10m window). - Added migration docs and dashboards for ops.

Why: this enables teams to correlate model changes and quantization/kv-cache strategies with direct unit economics and latency impact, enabling automated recommendations in Redwood Optimize and better on-call signal for regressions.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind obs.token_kv_metrics flag; rollout to staging on 2026-02-20, canary in us-west on 2026-02-21, full rollout after 48h if no regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Instrument metrics in runtime - [x] Add Prometheus scrape/testing - [x] Dashboard JSON and panels - [x] Alert rules and thresholds - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Backfill plan for 7 days of samples (prometheus retention)

Notes: Metric cardinality was carefully limited (model, region, customer_tier, short_prefix) to prevent explosion. We used continuous-bucketing for latency histograms to keep ingestion cost predictable. Related linear: ENG-4827, ENG-4890. Related support ticket: SUP-9182.

performance_impact: Observability overhead: ~0.6% p50 CPU on CPU sidecar, negligible GPU overhead
KV hit/miss metrics are sampled at prefix granularity to keep cardinality low
Initial canary showed 7% reduction in tail latency for requests benefiting from KV cache improvements due to faster detection and tuning
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache and token-cost observability: new metrics, Grafana dashboard, and tuned alerts. Rollout behind feature flag obs.token_kv_metrics; no breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag obs.token_kv_metrics on the prometheus/prometheus-config; ensure prometheus retention >=7d for default backfills. If KV hit-rate alerts fire, investigate recent model rollouts or quantization changes and consult runbook OBS-02.
